title: introduce-retrodictive-token-cost-and-alert-certainty-matrix
author: Leah Morrison
description: Background: token-level cost and latency telemetry is noisy for streamed / partial responses and multi-stage pipelines. This makes alerting brittle: small bursts or partial traces can spike cost-derived SLOs and generate false positives. This PR adds a retrodictive cost model that imputes per-token cost for partially observed invocations, and a new Alert Certainty Matrix that converts noisy signals into a calibrated certainty score used by alerting rules. Goals: 1) reduce alert churn for transient/partial traces, 2) improve cost attribution accuracy for streamed responses, 3) expose a dashboard that helps SREs inspect certainty vs. observed deltas. Implementation summary: - Add a lightweight retrodictor service (observability/cost/retrodictor.go) that uses invocation phase durations, kernel occupancy, and observed token counts to estimate final token counts and cost when traces are incomplete. It exposes a small protobuf/gRPC API and an internal REST shim for the console. - Emit a new span tag token_cost_estimate and token_cost_certainty on invocation spans; add a metric cost_certainty_bucket for rollups. - Introduce an Alert Certainty Matrix processor in telemetry pipeline that consumes the retrodictor output and materializes a certainty score (0.0-1.0) and a small explanation vector for debugging. - Console: dashboard panels showing certainty vs. actual cost, a scatterplot of certainty vs. latency, and an alert tuning view to set minimum certainty thresholds per route. - Alerting: default SLO alerts now reference certainty score; low-confidence alerts are suppressed to a separate queue and annotated. Rollout plan: staged rollout (console feature flag), canary telemetry pipeline with sampling, and a backward-compatible opt-out label for customers. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4187) - [x] Unit tests for retrodictor estimator - [x] End-to-end integration tests in telemetry sandbox - [x] Dashboard JSON and visual QA - [x] Documentation updates (observability docs) Commits: ["init: add retrodictor service skeleton and proto", "impl: estimator heuristics and kernel occupancy hooks", "metrics: emit token_cost_estimate & token_cost_certainty", "pipeline: add certainty matrix processor", "console: add certainty dashboard panels and tuning UI", "tests: add unit & e2e tests", "docs: add observability guide section"] Changed files (high level): ["observability/cost/retrodictor.go", "observability/cost/proto/retrodictor.proto", "telemetry/pipeline/certainty_matrix_processor.go", "telemetry/tests/retrodictor_e2e_test.go", "console/dashboards/cost_certainty_dashboard.json", "console/routes/alert_tuning_certainty.tsx", "otel/span_enrichment/token_cost_tags.go", "docs/observability/cost-certainty.md", "scripts/ci-retrodictor-lint.sh", "Makefile"] CI: initial run failed lint (golangci) and a flaky integration test; fixed lint issues and adjusted test timeout. Final CI checks: ["golangci-lint: pass", "unit-tests: pass", "e2e-sandbox: pass", "dashboard-qa: pass", "security-scan: pass"] Reviews & conversation: ["Evan Lee: Please add a note about potential bias for short-lived streams; can we add a conservative fallback?", "Leah Morrison: Added conservative fallback (returns 0.8 certainty lower bound) and documented assumptions in docs/observability/cost-certainty.md", "Marta Gomez: LGTM for telemetry pipeline; please ensure metrics cardinality guard is present", "Leah Morrison: Added cost_certainty_bucket as low-cardinality histogram and a guard in pipeline config", "Noah Patel: Can we surface the certainty explanation in trace view?", "Leah Morrison: Added span enrichment with a short explanation summary and a console trace overlay to show the explanation vector"] Migration notes: Existing alert rules remain unchanged until tenant opts into certainty-aware alerts via console toggle; the telemetry pipeline supports a compatibility mode that preserves previous metric names. Rollout: canary tenants (5%) -> ramp to 50% over 3 days -> global. Merge outcome: squash and merge after approvals and green CI. Related: touches routing of token attributor and small perf hooks in kernel occupancy sampler. This PR intentionally keeps estimator simple; future work will iterate with ML-backed retrodictor when we have ground-truth samples.
